study_identification_part.si4_title: Probing individual-level structural atrophy in frontal glioma patients

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To investigate individual-level non-tumoral structural atrophy patterns in frontal glioma patients, commonalities among these patterns, and their correlation with tumor characteristics, utilizing a developed individual-level structural abnormality detection method.

While T2-FLAIR was collected for patients, it was specifically for tumor segmentation and not for building the normative model from healthy controls. The normative model was built from T1 images.

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: Computational Anatomy Toolbox 12 (CAT12); SPM12; skull stripping; bias-field inhomogeneities correction; segmentation into GM, WM, CSF; MNI space normalization (optimized shooting algorithm); 4-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel smoothing.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The 'Brain volume extraction' section explicitly lists the software, steps, and algorithms used for processing the T1 images.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: Individual T1 images were processed using the Computational Anatomy Toolbox 12 (CAT12, http://dbm.neuro.uni-jena.de/cat/, Structural Brain Imaging Group, University of Jena, GER) to calculate the brain tissue volume. First, skull stripping and correction for bias-field inhomogeneities were performed. Then, the whole brain image was segmented into different tissue types, e.g., gray matter (GM), white matter (WM) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), followed by normalization of the segmented GM and WM images into the MNI space using optimized shooting algorithm [16]. Finally, the normalized GM and WM images were smoothed with a 4-mm full width at half maxima (FWHM) Gaussian kernel.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Spearman correlation was used to correlate abnormality indexes with continuous variables (tumor volume, CCI, MOCA score). Two-sample t-test was used for categorical variables (TERT mutation, 1p/19q co-deletion, MGMT promoter methylation, histological grade, IDH1). Significance level of p < 0.05 with false discovery rate (FDR) correction for multiple comparisons.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Glioma patients displayed unique and shared non-tumoral structural atrophy patterns, with several individual structural abnormality indexes serving as potential indicators of glioma molecular biomarkers.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Every glioma patient showed a unique atrophy pattern, with common overlapping gray matter (GM) atrophies in the temporal lobe (hippocampus, amygdala, parahippocampus, middle/inferior temporal gyrus, precuneus, lingual gyrus, fusiform, insula), with right temporal lobe atrophy more extensive. Overlapping white matter (WM) atrophies were mainly in bilateral thalamus and pallidum, with the contralateral side having larger atrophy. GM/WM relative atrophy ratio negatively correlated with tumor size. WM contralateral atrophy ratio differed significantly between IDH wild type and mutation type, and WM relative atrophy ratio differed with 1p/19q co-deletion status. Both GM/WM relative atrophy ratios showed differences between TERT wild type and mutation type.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: The optimal threshold for W is unclear; sex and TIV were not well matched between glioma patients and healthy controls; perifocal edema included during tumor segmentation may affect WM-related structural abnormality indexes.
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: There are several limitations of this study. First, the optimal threshold for W is not clear; we chose |W|> 6 in order to reduce the whole brain false positives in the detection of atrophy patterns. Second, the sex and TIV are not well matched between glioma patients and healthy controls. Third, in order to include a complete tumor-infiltrated area, the perifocal edema (high signal in T2-FLAIR) was included during the segmentation of tumor region. However, the perifocal edema may affect the WM related structural abnormality indexes, especially in high grade lesions.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study provides an effective way to access individual-level non-tumoral structural abnormalities in glioma patients, with potential for improving individualized precision medicine and presurgical evaluation and postsurgical prognosis. The methodology involved developing a modified W-score map and proposing several whole-brain GM/WM atrophy indexes.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study utilized W-scores to quantify individual-level deviation from a normative model of healthy controls, generating structural abnormality maps (SAMs) for gray matter (GM) and white matter (WM). Eight structural abnormality indexes were defined based on these SAMs. The code for the individual structural abnormality map and the datasets are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request. The study was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Beijing Tiantan Hospital and registered at Chinese ClinicalTrial Registry (ChiCTR2000031805).
